newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Firm stg to curb UK consumer boom.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Firm stg to curb UK consumer boom.

text.p: The strong pound will stop UK consumer spending overheating in 1997, as it hits industry and investment, and higher interest rates will also curb spending, Oxford Economic Forecasting said in a report on Friday.

Several factors point to a spending boom, such as tax cuts, lower unemployment and "windfalls', which will boost consumer spending by four percent this year, it said. But it said sterling's rise will make UK exports less competitive, squeezing export-oriented companies' profits and forcing them to cut capital investment.
As a result, Oxford Economic expects investment to rise by only four percent this year, below the Treasury's forecast of six.
It expects GDP growth to be held back at 3.3 percent in 1997 after a 2.4 percent rise in 1996.

Britain's trade balance is likely to suffer, with strong domestic demand accelerating imports and the rising pound dampening exports, it said. The current account deficit is likely to widen to 3.6 billion stg in 1997 from one billion in 1996, it said.
The institute expects Britain to raise interest rates by 25 basis points soon due to increasing inflationary pressures.

"Whichever party is in power from next May (after the general election), almost their first move will have to be to tighten monetary policy further, with interest rates rising to seven percent by next summer," it said.
